Hi Lena,

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. Per our conversation I put together three compact reservation structures we think will map well to Helia Health's expected burst/steady mix — the goal is to minimize committed spend during the pilot while preserving headroom for predictable growth into H1.

Attached: proposal_draft_v3.pdf (term summary) and capacity_model_helia.xlsx (cost/throughput math). TL;DR below: 

1) Micro-floor (12 GPU baseline) — fast onramp, low monthly commit, best for high-burst/low-24x7 needs. Includes 20% burst credit pool and automated burst-to-hosted fallback.

2) Staggered Staircase (24 -> 48 over 6 months) — lower initial commit, defined ramp triggers tied to monthly token thresholds and latency SLOs. Good balance of cost predictability + runway.

3) Anchored Slate (36 GPU baseline with 10% reserve) — for teams that want consistent throughput and simplified pricing; includes 99.9% uptime SLA and priority scheduling windows.

Specific ask: can you confirm the preferred ramp cadence (conservative vs. aggressive) and whether procurement expects a single PO or staged POs? That will change the contract cadence and the onboarding timeline (we've kept the onboarding window at 3–6 weeks depending on lane).

Thanks,

Kimberly

Thanks for the asks, Lena — looping in the ramp-trigger table and a short tech note on warm starts. Attaching an excerpt from capacity_model_helia.xlsx (tab: triggers). Quick summary: 

- Staggered Staircase triggers (recommended):
  * Step 1 (24 GPUs -> 36 GPUs): sustained 14-day average token consumption >= 65% of 24-GPU throughput AND 95th percentile latency > 350ms on the steady traffic profile.
  * Step 2 (36 GPUs -> 48 GPUs): sustained 30-day average token consumption >= 75% of 36-GPU throughput OR repeated SLO breaches (3 incidents in 14 days).

- Warm-start behavior for Micro-floor: we recommend enabling prefix KV caching + a short pre-warm window (30–60 seconds) that reduces cold-start p95 by ~40–55% for common inference pipelines. If Helia can accept a short (<1 min) pre-warm handshake on heavy batch windows, cold start impact is negligible for user-facing flows.

- Contracting impact: staged POs are supported; pricing tiers vary slightly based on committed term. Our proposal assumes a 12-month term for the Anchored Slate pricing; the Staircase uses a blended rate with early ramp credits (we've represented that in the proposal_draft_v3.pdf). Staged POs will not increase unit rates if total committed GPU-months meet the agreed floor over the first 6 months.
